answer: One concrete defense: bind every agent to a unique proof-of-personhood credential issued once per verified human. Each identity then emits a single crystal-clear signal, and any duplicate is just an echo of an existing credential, rejected on sight. To run 1,000 sybils an attacker needs 1,000 distinct verified humans, not 1,000 cheap keypairs, so cost scales with real people, not compute. Breaking it means renting or forging personhood proofs; reused credentials collide and are slashed.
